notes: Only the two instruction pages were supplied (no inventory pages), so Element IDs are best-guess matches from the catalogue by shape and colour. Treat part types and exact ports as approximate.
Small details in steps 3-7 (small deck plates, the blue and black seat bits, the dark-smoke window pieces) are low-resolution, so some small pieces may be missing or mis-typed.
The 'POLICE' print is a sticker, not modelled except the printed radar tile.

Step 1: one wheel-holder plate looks already fitted at one chassis end, so both holders are modelled as separate parts on the chassis. The chassis is typed lego-4287280 (many studs) so each part gets its own stud; the true chassis piece is uncertain.

Rear and front bumper sub-assemblies (white bracket, two lenses, dark base) are built the same way with different lens colours (red at the rear, yellow at the front). They are separate parts, not a repeat. Each base sits on the chassis and each bracket sits on its base.

The four wheels (white rim plus black tyre) are one repeat: two rims on the rear holder (b13), two on the front holder (b14, via attach overrides). Each wheel's pin-to-rim joint uses null ports because the catalogue's rim and pin port kinds do not pair cleanly.

The booklet really builds three separate models: the minifigure with walkie-talkie (b1-b5), the speed-camera stand (b6-b11) and the car (b12-b42, plus wheels). They are not physically connected in the instructions (the minifig and stand are only shown beside the finished car), so they stay as three separate groups on purpose.

Minifig joins (cap-head, head-torso, torso-legs, torso-walkie-talkie) and the pole-to-clip joins use null ports because the catalogue port kinds do not match (socket/stud, anti-stud/pin). The light bar base joins the roof with a null port because the roof's two studs are used by the antennas. Legs use catalogue part lego-4551179 (police legs, black) because the previous IDs were rejected as not real. The police cap is a new type because no catalogue entry matches it.
